President Rinkēvičs confirmed it was a Ukrainian drone targeting Russian objectives that went off course. Latvia issued diplomatic protest to Russia.

story_clusters.headline: PM Siliņa and Hungarian PM Orbán engage in public social media dispute over Ukraine support
story_clusters.summary: PM Evika Siliņa and Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán exchanged critical posts on social media about EU financial support for Ukraine and Russian oil deliveries through the Druzhba pipeline. Siliņa accused Hungary of blocking Ukraine aid to maintain Russian oil imports.

story_clusters.headline: Major IT procurement corruption scandal emerges with arrests and European Prosecutor involvement
story_clusters.summary: European Prosecutor's Office launched criminal investigation into suspected fraud in 1.5 million euro IT procurement contracts. Former VDAA director Jorens Liopa arrested. Investigation affects election systems and raises concerns about democratic processes.

story_clusters.headline: President calls for manual vote counting in upcoming Saeima elections
story_clusters.summary: President Rinkēvičs announced that votes in October's parliamentary elections should be counted manually due to concerns about IT procurement fraud affecting election systems. New legislation passed to ensure manual counting procedures.

story_clusters.headline: Government reduces diesel excise tax to address rising fuel prices
story_clusters.summary: Cabinet approved 15% reduction in diesel excise tax to help stabilize fuel prices amid Middle East conflict impact. PM Siliņa urged public to use public transport more while government considers additional measures if prices continue rising.

story_clusters.headline: Defense Minister Sprūds visits Ukraine, delivers weapons and discusses drone cooperation
story_clusters.summary: Defense Minister Andris Sprūds met with Ukrainian President Zelensky and Defense Minister Fedorov in Kyiv. Latvia delivered CVR(T) armored vehicles and Natrix land drones to Ukraine. Both sides signed agreements on defense industry cooperation including joint drone production.

story_clusters.headline: Saeima passes stricter immigration controls for third-country nationals
story_clusters.summary: Parliament approved in final reading significant amendments to Immigration Law imposing stricter conditions on foreign nationals living in Latvia. Changes include restrictions on food delivery platform cooperation with third-country couriers and enhanced monitoring of compliance.

story_clusters.headline: President Rinkēvičs publishes annual asset declaration showing significant savings increase
story_clusters.summary: President Rinkēvičs' annual declaration shows his cash savings increased by 72,779 euros to 251,924 euros in 2025. He earned 105,109 euros in presidential salary and made several bond investments totaling 200,000 euros.
